topic: Lambda Capture Reference: Dangling Reference Risk
explanation: Assumption: Capturing a local stack variable by reference (`[&var]` or default `[&]`) is safe as long as the lambda is used immediately. Reality: The closure object resulting from the lambda expression may be stored in a container or returned, allowing its lifetime to exceed the scope of the captured automatic variable. Why It Fails: When the surrounding function exits, its stack frame is destroyed, and the local variable ceases to exist. The closure object still holds a reference (pointer) to that now-invalid memory location. Any subsequent invocation of the stored lambda results in Undefined Behavior (accessing a dangling reference).
practical_example: A developer writes a class method that generates and stores a validation lambda into a member container. If the lambda captures a temporary local variable or a function parameter by reference, invoking that validator later (after the method returns) will likely lead to a crash or memory corruption.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
